text:
emma-rt: FYI canary (r-dedicated-east) token/sec dropped ~32% after merge a2f4c8. Perf bot also flagged CI perf. Looks like continuous-batcher behavior changed. /cc @rajv @oliver :eyes:
perf-bot: CI perf regression detected on benchmarks/long_seq. tokens/sec -28% (build 9823). Details: https://ci.internal/reports/9823 :warning:
rajv: On it. Spinning up pprof and scheduler traces now. Any config diffs in that merge?
oliver: I grabbed a quick flame and scheduler trace. Avg batch_size jumped from ~14 -> ~28 and queue_wait p50 increased from 12ms -> 85ms. KV cache hit-rate also down ~9%. Paste: 
```
# scheduler summary
avg_batch_size: 27.8
queue_wait_p50_ms: 85
queue_wait_p95_ms: 360
kv_cache_hitrate: 0.78 -> 0.69
tokens/sec_canary: 420k -> 286k
```
rajv: Interesting — merge a2f4c8 bumped the adaptive padding logic (pad_fraction default 0.15 -> 0.4) and enabled prefetch-padding for CTB. That could explain bigger batches and extra KV prefetch traffic.
kim: If padding increases, we get larger batches but also more KV cache churn + longer tail waits (stragglers) -> net tokens/sec drop.
emma-rt: Can we bisect to confirm the offending diff? If it's config change, revert should be quick.
rajv: Starting bisect now: `git bisect start --term-old=good --term-new=bad; git bisect good v1.9.2; git bisect bad HEAD`
oliver: While bisect runs, I ran a targeted local repro with the new pad_fraction and saw identical throughput loss. Reproduced with --ctb-prefetch-padding enabled.
rajv: Bisect points to commit a2f4c8 (the padding + prefetch switches). Confirmed.
kim: Proposed mitigation: revert the config/default or gate prefetch with feature flag for canary. Which is faster?
emma-rt: Rollback the merge on canary first (hold rollout). I'll open a revert PR and patch default.
perf-bot: deploy-bot: Revert PR created (#3489) and deploy to r-dedicated-east started.
oliver: After revert applied, quick measurements show tokens/sec recovering: 410k -> 436k (small +6% vs pre-incident). queue_wait_p50 back to ~14ms. KV hit-rate restored to ~0.77.
rajv: Root cause summary: adaptive padding increase + prefetch-padding caused excessive padding per request, inflating batch sizes and KV prefetch ops. That increased queueing and KV cache thrash, reducing overall tokens/sec.
kim: Action items:
- revert default pad_fraction change (done)
- gate prefetch-padding behind feature flag + add canary config (in progress)
- add perf unit test for tokens/sec sensitivity to pad_fraction (ticket #INF-1212)
- postmortem if rollout to prod happened (monitoring shows only canary affected)

emma-rt: thanks everyone. marking rollout hold until feature flag + perf tests in place. :white_check_mark:
